Alan: 'I think there should be a separate page for screenshots of each section of the application that explains
what is happening instead of just a few screenshots on the main page.' A handful of pictures on the home page
shows that GroupLab exists. It does not show what using it is like, and that is the question somebody has before
This file is the list. website/build.py builds the index and one page per screen from it, and refuses to build if
a screen here has no screenshot or a screenshot has no screen here, so the tour and the weekly screenshot job of
entry 144 section 4 cannot drift apart quietly.
Every 'part' must name something a reader can actually see in the picture, in the words the screen itself uses.
No class names, no file paths, and nothing claimed that is not in the build the pictures came from.
Entry 152: what each screen does with a target GroupLab did not print is a field of its own, 'withoutASheet',
and every screen has one. On several of them the honest answer is 'no difference', and saying so is worth a line.
docs/WHAT-CAN-BE-MEASURED.md is the one source for what GroupLab can measure and where the scale comes from;
nothing here states its own version of that.
Entry 155: the Target library and Printing were two screens doing one job, and are one screen now, Targets. /tour/library/ and
/tour/print/ are each a plain page with one link to /tour/targets/, since entry 151 bans a meta refresh, so a link to either still arrives.

marking.name: Marking and review
marking.blurb: Every hole found and numbered to its bull, with anything uncertain raised for you to settle.
marking.purpose: This is where GroupLab shows its working before it measures anything. It finds the holes, works out the scale from the printed markers, and assigns each hole to a bull. Where it is not sure, it says so and asks, rather than quietly guessing and giving you a clean-looking number built on a guess.
marking.withoutASheet: The same screen, and the work is yours. You set the scale, by tapping a known length or the corners of a known rectangle, and you place each shot. There is no automatic detection, nothing is assigned to a bull for you, and the review queue stays empty, because it exists to question what the detector decided and nothing decided anything.
parts: Setup, at the top of the panel

Caliber, shot distance and rounds fired come first, each saying in a line what it unlocks. One that matters and is still empty is outlined and says needed, until you answer it or say not known. Rifle, barrel and load, the paper and what was behind it sit under them.
The count at the top
How many shots are marked and how many need review, so you know how much is left before you can trust the result.
Review, on the right

One question at a time, in order, each saying what GroupLab thinks and why. The buttons are the answers. Here it has found 24 marks on a sheet that takes 25, nobody has said how many rounds were fired, and it has put its best candidate first with the evidence for it.
The numbered list underneath
Every question still to answer, the current one marked NOW and the next marked NEXT.
The keyboard line

C pans and V selects, side by side under the left hand. Space moves to the next item, Enter takes the first choice, a bull's number reassigns the selected shot, N marks it not a shot. Faster than the mouse once a sheet has a dozen questions.
Selected shot

Everything known about the one you have picked: where it is, how wide the hole is, how many holes' worth of ink it contains, and how far it is from anything else. The three chips say whether it was detected, corrected by you, or added by hand.
Called flyer and Exclude
Marking a shot you called as a flyer, or leaving it out of the measurement. GroupLab keeps it on the sheet and says so in the analysis rather than deleting it.
Scale

Which markers gave the scale and how many of them were read, and for a photograph how far off square it was and how good it is. This is what makes the measurement real, so it is shown rather than assumed.
Find the paper's edges

With the rectangle tool, on a target GroupLab did not print: the paper's four corners placed for you when the sheet stands out from what is behind it, and a standard paper size offered when the photograph's shape matches one.
The tools along the top of the picture

Pan, which is the tool on open and also selects a mark you click without moving it, then measure, box, the scale ends, the bull picker, and select, which is the one that drags a mark. Undo and redo sit beside them.
Detect on a GroupLab sheet
Runs the detection again, for instance after you have entered the caliber.
Accept and analyze
When you are satisfied. It saves the session and takes you to the analysis.
steps: Open your photograph or scan, by dragging it onto the window or from the file menu.
Answer the setup at the top: the caliber, the distance and how many rounds you fired, or say not known.
Answer each review item in turn, using the buttons or the keys shown.
Drag any mark that sits off a hole with the select tool, V, and use a bull's number to move a shot to the right bull.
Mark anything you called as a flyer, then press Accept and analyze.
marking.fits: After you have shot and photographed a sheet from Targets. It leads to the analysis.

analysis.name: The analysis
analysis.blurb: Every shot on one bull, with the six figures a shooter reads in view and everything else one click away.
analysis.purpose: Twenty-five bulls shot one round each become one picture of twenty-five shots, because each shot is measured from its own bull. Every number here comes with an interval, which is the range the true value could really be given how few shots you fired. That is the difference between knowing a load is better and hoping it is.
analysis.withoutASheet: No difference. Every figure here is worked out from the marks and the scale, and it does not matter whether a detector placed them or you did.
parts: Back, top left
Returns to marking with every edit as you left it.
The composite, in the middle

A dot at each shot's center, drawn where it landed relative to its own bull, on white with dark outlines at the hole size, so it reads on a laptop in daylight. The group center and the extreme spread line are the one color that stands out.
The key, top left

What each mark means, listing only what is shown: the shots, the red extreme spread line, the green CEP circles (50 dotted, 90 solid, 95 dashed), the green lines through the group center and the blue lines through where you aimed. Toggles beside the plot turn CEP 50, 90 and 95 and the extreme spread on and off, and Group or Whole target frames the group alone or the entire bull; GroupLab remembers both. The wheel or a pinch zooms, dragging empty paper moves the view, and a double click fits it again.
Zero correction

How far the group center is from where you aimed, across and up and down, in inches, MOA and mil side by side, and the distance the correction is for. Beneath it one line says what to dial, in clicks of your scope with the click value, or that the offset cannot yet be told from chance. Its why holds the give or take.
Group

Center from aim, extreme spread, group width by height, mean radius, and CEP 50 and 90. With the shot distance set each is an angle first, in MOA unless you chose another unit, with its size on the paper beneath; without it, the size on the paper and a button to set the distance. Hover over a figure for the range it could really be and the figure without any shot you left out.
Advanced, closed until you open it

Sigma, the strips across and up and down, the order fired, the shape and flyer tests, the full CEP table, sighters, and carrying the correction to another distance. GroupLab remembers whether you opened it.
The scale badge
Scale checked, with a tick, when the sheet's own markers set the scale. The detail is behind Show work.
The load block, left
Which rifle, barrel, load and caliber this sheet was shot with, and where the caliber came from.
Shots, from their own bull
Every shot as numbers, across, up and down, and radius. The widest pair is picked out in bold.
Own window, Show work, Report and Export

Own window moves the figures to a window of their own for a second monitor. Show work opens how the sheet was read. Report makes a printable page. Export writes the complete record, or the shot coordinates as CSV for a spreadsheet.
steps: Read the mean radius, and hover over it for the range it could really be.
Check the zero correction and the line under it saying what to dial, or that the offset is not real yet at this many shots.
Open Advanced for the strips across and up and down, and the tests.
Report or Export if you want to keep it outside GroupLab.
analysis.fits: After marking. The session is saved to session records, where two can be sent to compare loads.

analysis-open.name: Showing the work
analysis-open.blurb: The same analysis with every explanation opened, so no number on the screen is one you have to take on trust.
analysis-open.purpose: Every figure GroupLab shows has a why beside it. This is the analysis with all of them open at once. It exists because a measurement you cannot check is a measurement you cannot argue with, and the whole point of measuring a group is to settle an argument about a load.
analysis-open.withoutASheet: No difference. The explanations are of the arithmetic, which is the same either way, except that the scale is named as the one you set.
parts: The why links
Beside every figure on the analysis. Each opens the reasoning for that one number: what was measured, over how many shots, and what the interval means.
Show work, at the top
Opens all of them together, which is this view.
The review notice
Where decisions were left unmade in marking, it says how many and offers to take you back to them, because an analysis over unsettled marks is worth less than one over settled ones.
steps: Press Show work on the analysis.
Read the reasoning beside any number you are about to act on.
Press it again to fold them away.
analysis-open.fits: The same screen as the analysis, with everything opened.

sessions.name: Session records
sessions.blurb: Every sheet you have accepted, newest first, ready to open again or to compare.
sessions.purpose: A session is one sheet, accepted and saved. This is the list of them. It is how you go back to a result weeks later, and how you pick which two loads to put side by side.
sessions.withoutASheet: No difference. A session from a hand-marked target is saved, listed and reopened like any other.
parts: Rifle and Load
Narrow the list to one rifle or one load. Choosing a single load also shows whether it is getting better or worse over time.
The tick boxes
Choose two or more sessions to compare.
The columns
Date, sheet, rifle, load, distance, how many shots, and the mean radius with its interval, so you can see at a glance which sessions are worth comparing without opening any of them.
Compare the chosen
Takes the ticked sessions to the compare screen.
A row
Opens that session's analysis again, exactly as it was.
Delete
Removes one session. It does not touch the image it was made from.
steps: Filter by rifle or load if the list is long.
Tick the sessions you want to put beside each other.
Press Compare the chosen, or click a row to reopen its analysis.
sessions.fits: Filled by the analysis every time you accept a sheet. Feeds compare loads.

compare.name: Compare loads
compare.blurb: Two or more sessions side by side, and a plain sentence saying whether the shots actually tell them apart.
compare.purpose: This is the screen that answers the question load development is for. It puts the groups beside each other, then draws each measurement as the range it could really be. Where those ranges overlap, the shots have not told the loads apart, and it says so in words rather than leaving you to read it off a chart.
compare.withoutASheet: No difference, with one thing worth knowing: a hand-set scale that assumes a square-on photograph carries that assumption into the comparison, and the figures say so.
parts: The plots along the top

One per load. Dots are the shots about their own bulls, excluded ones left out; the green lines cross at the group center and the blue lines at the aim point, with the green CEP circles the analysis screen's toggles have on.
The figures under each plot
Sigma, mean radius and extreme spread, each with its 95 percent interval.
Mean radius, with the range each could really be
A line per load showing the whole interval, with the measured value marked on it. Two lines that overlap are two loads these shots cannot separate.
The sentence underneath
The conclusion in plain words. Here: every one of these overlaps every other, so these shots do not tell them apart.
Sigma, with the range each could really be
The same treatment for the other measure of spread.
The header
How many loads, how many shots in total, and that they are in the order you chose.
steps: Tick two or more sessions in session records and press Compare the chosen.
Read the sentence under the mean radius bars before you read the numbers.
If the intervals overlap, shoot more of both loads rather than picking a winner.
Look at the plots for a difference in shape that the single numbers hide.
compare.fits: From session records. It is usually where a load development session ends.
links: Was it the wind or the rifle

equipment.name: Equipment
equipment.blurb: Your rifles, barrels and loads. A sheet names one of each, and everything else takes what it needs from here.
equipment.purpose: Rather than typing the same rifle into every session, you record it once. Everything is optional except a name: GroupLab will happily measure a group for a rifle it knows nothing else about. The extra fields are there because the ballistics page and the zero correction need them, and it says which one is missing when it cannot work something out.
equipment.withoutASheet: No difference. Nothing here depends on a sheet.
parts: Rifles, Barrels, Loads
Three lists behind three buttons. A session names one of each.
The list on the left
What you have already, with Add another underneath.
The form on the right
Name is the only field you must fill in. Sight height and Zeroed at are the two the zero correction uses; twist, scope and click value matter for the ballistics page.
Notes
Anything that does not fit a field. It travels with the record.
The line along the bottom
A reminder that nothing here changes a marking. A sheet names which of these it was shot with, and that is all.
steps: Add a rifle with just its name if that is all you have.
Fill in sight height and the distance it is zeroed at when you want zero corrections.
Add the load, with muzzle velocity and ballistic coefficient if you want a dope table.
Press Save. The record is then offered on every new session.
equipment.fits: Used by marking, the analysis and ballistics.

ballistics.name: Ballistics
ballistics.blurb: A trajectory for one rifle and load, a dope table at whatever spacing you ask for, and the chance of a hit from your own measured precision.
ballistics.purpose: Everything else in GroupLab measures what your rifle did. This works out what it should do. It takes the rifle and load you have already recorded, asks for the air it will be shot in, and gives you drop, wind drift, velocity and energy out to whatever distance you name, and the chance of a hit there from your own measured precision. Nothing here changes a marking or an analysis.
ballistics.withoutASheet: No difference. Nothing here depends on a sheet.
parts: Units
Imperial or metric, for this page.
Rifle and Load
Chosen from what you recorded on the equipment screen. The fields below fill themselves in from those records.
The rifle
Sight height, zero distance, barrel twist and its direction. Twist is what lets it work out spin drift.
The load
Muzzle velocity and its standard deviation, ballistic coefficient, drag model and the atmosphere the coefficient was measured in, bullet weight, length and diameter.
The air
Temperature, station pressure, altitude and humidity. Leave the pressure empty to take it from the altitude.
Keep these on the records
Writes what you have typed back to the rifle and load, so you do not type it again.
Dope table
To what distance, and in what steps. Work out the table fills the chart.
Drop, Wind drift, Velocity, Energy
Four views of the same trajectory. The chart marks your zero.
The analyzed group at another distance
The group open in the analysis carried through the solver to a distance you name, labeled a prediction, with its sigma there and its interval.
Hit probability

The chance of a hit on a circle, a rectangle or an IPSC outline, from the rifle precision you measured, the load's velocity spread and a confidence preset for everything nobody can measure. First and second round sit beside the elevation and wind for the distance, each with its interval.
What costs the most
Every error source by the hits it takes away, so you can see whether the wind call, the load or the range estimate is what to work on.
Advanced
Each uncertainty the preset set, a bias beside it for something you know is off, the zero error, the latitude, and the trials and seed that make a result repeatable.
steps: Choose the rifle and load.
Fill in anything the record is missing; the page names the field when it cannot solve.
Set the air, or leave the pressure empty and give the altitude.
Set the distance and step, press Work out the table, and switch between drop, drift, velocity and energy.
For a hit probability, set the distance and the target, choose the confidence preset closest to your situation, and press Work out the chance.
ballistics.fits: Takes its inputs from equipment. It does not feed back into a marking or an analysis.

settings.name: Settings
settings.blurb: Units, theme, which builds it offers you, and the log. Every choice here is remembered.
settings.purpose: Short by design. The units change how every figure is displayed and nothing that is stored, so you can switch between inches and millimeters without touching a single record. The rest is about this build: what it is, whether it looks for a newer one, and how to send a problem report.
settings.withoutASheet: No difference. Nothing here depends on a sheet.
parts: Units
Lengths, angles and distances. Displayed only; nothing stored changes. A box beneath puts a group's size on the paper before its angle, for shooting at one distance.
Theme
Light, dark, or follow the system.
This build
The version and the commit it was made from. Copy that line into a bug report and it says exactly which build you were on.
Updates
Which train to follow and how often to check. A check is one request for one public file, and it sends nothing about you, your rifles or your targets.
Error reports
Whether a report of an error goes to the project by itself, you are asked each time, or it never goes, and what a report holds. Not switched on yet, and until it is nothing is sent.
Sending targets

Whether each target you analyze goes to the project, you are asked each time, or it never goes, and with which consent. What is sent, how many targets have gone from this computer and how to have one removed are here too.
Detailed logging
Off by default. Turn it on before reproducing a problem, then send the report.
Report a problem
Collects what is useful and lets you look at it before anything leaves your machine.
steps: Set your units once. Everything on every screen follows.
Choose a theme, or leave it following the system.
If you are testing, set the train to nightly so you are offered new builds.
Turn on detailed logging only while chasing a problem.
settings.fits: Reachable from the cog at the bottom of the sidebar on every screen.

targets.name: Targets
targets.blurb: The {count:sheets} sheets GroupLab comes with and any you design, grouped by what they are for, and everything it takes to print the one you choose, on one screen.
targets.merged: This was two screens, the target library and printing. They did the same job, so they are one screen now.
targets.purpose: This is where you choose which sheet to print and print it. Every sheet is designed for a particular job at a particular distance, and the description under each says which. A GroupLab sheet is the easy path, because it carries its own scale, its own orientation and the positions of its bulls in the markers printed around them, so nothing has to be set by hand. It prints at its true size. A sheet printed smaller than it should be is still read correctly, bull by bull, because the markers shrank with everything else. It matters for photographs, because a photograph cannot measure the print scale; a scan can and corrects for it. A scan measures the scale and reports every size in real inches; a photograph of a sheet printed at 97 percent makes every group read about 3 percent large. So this screen asks the PDF viewer for no scaling, prints the instruction along the bottom of the sheet so you can check with a ruler, and refuses outright when the paper cannot hold the sheet.
targets.withoutASheet: Nothing on this screen applies. It holds and prints GroupLab's own sheets; a target from anywhere else is opened on the marking screen instead.
parts: The list, grouped by what the sheet is for

Centerfire load development, rimfire, large format, long range on tiled pages, long range on roll media, and zeroing grids. A zeroing grid is for sighting in by eye at the bench, read off the grid after each shot; for a zero worked out from a group, and group figures, use a 5x5 sheet. The right hand column of each row is the paper size and how many scoring bulls it has, with the sighter bulls after the plus sign.
The sheet you have chosen, beside the list
Its name and full description: the bull spacing, the sighter row, the distance it was designed for, and the paper it wants. Choosing a sheet fills everything under it at once.
Built in and read only
The twenty that come with GroupLab cannot be edited. Duplicate makes a copy that is yours, to rename and change.
The load block
Blank, to write on at the range, or filled in now from its fields.
Print the actual-size instruction
Adds a line along the bottom edge of each sheet telling whoever prints it to choose Actual size and never Fit. Leave it on unless you are printing for yourself and know the driver.
Open to print, Save PDF and Print
Open to print hands the PDF to your usual viewer, which is the safest route today. Save PDF writes the file. Print goes straight to a driver, on Windows.
Print a volunteer pack
The sheet plus one page telling somebody else how to shoot it, photograph it and send it back.
Previous sheet, Next sheet
For a tiled sheet that spans several pages. The counter says which page of how many.
The preview, with Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit

The artwork of the page about to print, filling the rest of the screen. It is artwork, not a photograph, so it stays sharp however far you go in; its text is drawn in the PDF, so the preview shows slightly less than the paper will.
Design your own sheet
For a sheet no built-in one covers. The designer opens beside the list, and your own sheets appear at the bottom of it.
steps: Find the group that matches what you are doing: load development, rimfire, zeroing.
Pick a sheet whose distance and paper size match your range and your printer.
Leave the actual-size instruction on if anybody but you will print it.
Press Open to print, and in the print dialog choose Actual size or 100 percent, never Fit or Shrink oversized pages.
Measure one printed bull with a ruler against the size in the description before you shoot a whole session on it.
targets.fits: This is usually where a session starts. You shoot the sheet, then photograph or scan it and open it in marking.
